method: Static reverse engineering; specimens were not executed and embedded endpoints were not contacted.
external_lookup: The supplied Triage/Bazaar URLs were inaccessible through the web tool. Searches returned no corroborating results. Supplied reputations were treated as leads, not behavioral proof.

evidence: Extracted MSI OLE streams with olefile and its cabinet with 7zz; inspected the managed ClientService, Client, Windows and Core assemblies using dnfile/dncil IL disassembly. The cabinet has a damaged localization resource; analysis does not rely on that resource.

Service parameters and system.config pin relay.cornebrdjubf.top:8041 and an RSA public key. Core ClientLaunchParameters::FromQueryString at RVA 0x61dc decodes the query, copies parameters and enforces the supplied constraint.

ClientService::Start at RVA 0x2228 starts maintenance of client processes and the credential-provider server. ClientService::ProcessMessage implements the remote-management message and consent handling expected for this product.

app.config explicitly disables Support/Access control banners, connection/hide balloons and tray icons. Core ApplicationSettings::ShouldShowBalloonOnConnect at RVA 0x16295 and ShouldShowSystemTrayIcon at RVA 0x163d5 return false under these settings. This is real notification suppression and remains suspicious.

No Access/Guest role or explicit auto-consent override was found in the embedded deployment query. SERVICE_CLIENT_LAUNCH_PARAMETERS is an installer property, not evidence by itself of a consent policy.

The custom relay and suppressed UI warrant review, but these bytes do not establish unauthorized deployment, a malicious code addition or an authentication bypass. A repository label is insufficient to convict a legitimate remote-admin product.

Inspected imports, cross-references and disassembly using Rizin, and decompiled native functions using Ghidra. Product attribution is corroborated by the implemented ESET mirror behavior, not accepted solely from version resources.
Main at VA 0x4123c0 dispatches standby-mutate, autostart and mutate modes, creates the single-instance mutex, starts the mirror thread and registers timers.

VA 0x4127e4 opens the requested executable, seeks to EOF and appends 4..11 pseudorandom bytes. VA 0x415800 creates a standby copy and passes the original path/PID; VA 0x41416c waits, mutates the original and relaunches it with -no-rotate. The timer repeats rotation. Retain the suspicious self-hash-rotation finding.

VA 0x4159f8 writes the quoted current image path to HKLM CurrentVersion\Run; VA 0x4154cc invokes ShellExecuteW with runas and -autostart on failure. This requests UAC elevation and is not an elevation bypass.
VA 0x412fac binds 0.0.0.0:8000 and starts per-client handlers. On a busy port it enumerates TCP owners and terminates the owner; this aggressive port reclamation remains notable.

The handler at VA 0x4144fc parses HTTP request paths, rejects .signed resources, routes manifest paths to fixed ESET upstream paths, and relays through VA 0x414868. VA 0x417c40 strips SERVERS, LINKS and HOSTS sections from manifests. These transformations preserve the local update-mirror role and do not establish malicious payload substitution.

VA 0x415c80 fetches the account list, rotates trial-/eav- entries and validates them against um01.cn.eset.com. No victim credential store is read or exfiltrated. WinHTTP certificate relaxation is already reported as a notable capability.

VA 0x416bb0 decodes each byte as input XOR key XOR ((index*31+7)&255). Decoded constants are id.1yz.me, /id.html, encrypt and type. The constructed credential-list URL uses HTTPS port 4046; these are account-fetch configuration, not a command dispatcher.

VA 0x412964 fetches update metadata, compares versions and asks the user with MessageBoxW MB_YESNO before downloading/executing a replacement. Only MZ magic is checked, but the explicit user choice distinguishes this updater path from covert remote-command execution.

No observed path establishes theft, spying, destructive intent, a backdoor or user deception. Preserve unusual hash rotation and neutral registry, execution, relay and termination capabilities without adding an unsupported conviction.
Unpacked with UPX 5.2.1, then independently analyzed the unpacked PE using Rizin and Ghidra and collected cleave facts.

Every mapped section is byte-identical to the 16e7978135e3 sample: .text, .data, .rdata, .bss, .idata, .CRT, .tls and .rsrc. Differences are packaging/header/overlay data. The same execution-path analysis applies.

Stock UPX packing adds no hostile behavior. Preserve the verified self-hash mutation and relaunch finding; ordinary Run registration plus a runas reference establishes no additional suspicious persistence objective.

changes: Remove redundant self-mutating-elevated-run-autostart; keep hash rotation and notable startup/elevation observations separately.
Set third-party ScreenConnect product inventory to notable rather than suspicious.
Require ScreenConnect application-settings evidence for the hidden-indicator group; do not suppress the actual configuration merely because the package is signed or is an installer.
Require explicit role/consent evidence for the unattended-installer finding; service placeholders and disabled notifications no longer suffice.
Remove the duplicate hidden-indicator leg from the command-channel deployment composite.
Recognize generic h=name,p=number query fields in the URL-query capability leaf and combine with ScreenConnect constraint/key evidence to cover self-hosted relays.
Bind XML setting matchers to the first following value element so they cannot borrow another setting value.
controls: Nine XML positives/near misses exercise visible/hidden indicators, unrelated application context, neighboring values, disabled/enabled consent, cloud/self-hosted relays and missing ports. check.py also asserts zero hostile and exactly one distinct suspicious trait in each saved sample report.
